docs.title: State of the Art — AI & Time Series
docs.text:
Welcome to the public state of the art (SOTA) of the IEEE AI and Time Series Working Group (AITS-WG).

AITS-WG develops standards within the IEEE Standards Association (IEEE SA). It reports to the Artificial Intelligence Standards Committee (C/AISC) of the IEEE Computer Society, and works on two standards projects authorized by the IEEE SA Standards Board: IEEE P3579 and IEEE P3998, presented below. The references on these pages are the ones the working group collects for each project.

How a reference is classified under IEEE P3579, IEEE P3998 or both: see How references are classified.

docs.title: How references are classified
docs.text: In one line: does the AI system consume the time series, as an input it infers from or is trained on (→ IEEE P3579), or produce it, as a record of its own operation (→ IEEE P3998)?

docs.title: Q1. Is the AI system the consumer? → IEEE P3579
docs.text:
The AI system consumes the time series: the series comes from outside the AI system, which uses it in one of two ways.

  1. Inference. The AI system infers from the time series, for example by forecasting, detecting anomalies or classifying. This includes evaluating a model on held-out series.
  2. Training. The time series becomes training data to build an AI model, including fine-tuning.

This also covers the definition, format, acquisition and preprocessing of the series an AI system consumes, even when the reference involves no AI method. Modelling or analysis methods that do not rely on AI are out of scope.

docs.title: Q2. Is the AI system the producer? → IEEE P3998
docs.text:
The AI system produces the time series: the series is a time-stamped record that the AI system produces, or should produce, about its own operation during its life cycle. Examples are training logs and metrics, internal states, and inference events. This covers the records and their definition, timing or format. Defining what such a system should produce is the purpose of the standard.

What "produce" does not cover: a model's output, such as a forecast or a generated series, is not a record of the AI system's own operation. A forecasting model is therefore a consumer only. External series, synthetic series and data derived from the internal records are out of scope.

docs.title: Where a reference goes
docs.text:
Consumer (Q1) Producer (Q2) Where it goes yes no IEEE P3579 no yes IEEE P3998 yes yes Both: it appears on the P3579, P3998 and joint pages no no Not added

Examples:

  • Forecasting models and datasets: the AI system consumes the series → P3579.
  • Explainable AI for time-series classification: the classifier consumes the series → P3579.
  • Training loggers of reinforcement-learning agents: the AI system produces the logs → P3998.
  • A date-time or temporal format, such as ISO 8601 or OWL-Time, used both for the series an AI system consumes and for the records it produces → both.

docs.title: Adding a reference in Zotero
docs.text:
• P3579 only: add it to the IEEE-P3579 group.
  • P3998 only: add it to the IEEE-P3998 group.
  • Both: add it to one group, then, in Zotero desktop, drag it onto the same section of the other group. The joint page is built from the references present in both groups.

File a reference in a section that has no sub-sections. A reference filed on a section with sub-sections, or on no section, is not published.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
Authors Title Year DOI Notes — A2C — Logger — Stable Baselines3 2.8.0a4 documentation 📝 — PPO — Logger — Stable Baselines3 2.8.0a4 documentation 📝 💬 A2C — Logger — Stable Baselines3 2.8.0a4 documentation — Any AIS, during its lifecycle, produces temporally ordered data as a byproduct…

Any AIS, during its lifecycle, produces temporally ordered data as a byproduct of its operation. As a concrete illustration, the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) implementation in Stable-Baselines3 (SB3) includes a built-in logger that records, at each logging interval, a single snapshot grouping training metrics (loss, policy divergence), rollout statistics (mean reward, episode length), and temporal markers (iterations, elapsed time, total timesteps). These repeated snapshots form ordered sequences of values produced internally by the system, not consumed from an external source. However, these temporal markers remain relative counters and durations — not standardized timestamps. There is no formal temporal reference framework governing how these internal records are indexed, formatted, or exchanged. This is precisely the gap P3998 aims to address: defining a unified format for the temporal data records that AIS inherently produce but do not yet record in a standardized way. P3579 standardizes how AIS consume external time series; P3998 addresses the complementary direction — the internal temporal data records that AIS produce. Together, they cover both sides of the relationship between AIS and time series.

— jschneerson, 2026-03-26 · ↩ back to reference
